claims.judged: Does acute sleep deprivation impair reversal learning in mice?
claims.text: Well posed and answerable at this scale.

claims.judged: If it does, is the impairment mediated by reduced orbitofrontal activity?
The project will not test chronic sleep restriction or human participants.
Acute (24 h) sleep deprivation impairs reversal learning in mice.
The impairment is mediated by reduced orbitofrontal cortex activity during reversal.
claims.text: Mediation is asserted; the design measures activity, not mediation.

claims.judged: Sleep-deprived mice need more trials than controls to reach criterion after a reward-contingency reversal.
Sleep-deprived mice show fewer c-Fos-positive cells in orbitofrontal cortex after the reversal session.
claims.text: Consistent with h2 but does not test it against reduced engagement.

claims.judged: Two-choice odour discrimination with a single reward-contingency reversal; trials to criterion (8 of 10 correct) compared between 24 h sleep-deprived and rested
c-Fos immunostaining in lateral orbitofrontal cortex 90 min after the reversal session; positive-cell density compared between groups.
claims.text: Correlational; the scope claim s1 already concedes this.

claims.judged: c-Fos density cannot distinguish reduced orbitofrontal activity from reduced task engagement; the design bears on prediction p2 only correlationally.
claims.text: The proposal is honest about its limit.
A sound behavioural test with a weak mechanistic arm; fundable if the mechanistic claim is held provisional.
